summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of Trust Intake & Client Portal. 27/28 backend tests pass. Only failure: brute-force lockout test — RCA: server uses request.client.host which is the K8s ingress proxy IP and rotates across pods, so the per-IP counter never reaches 5 on a single pod. Frontend: admin login redirects to /admin, client register→portal→Single Trust→wizard flow works, hard-stop validation enforced (Next disabled when incomplete, future steps locked), messaging in wizard works.

critical.issue: Lockout never triggers in deployed env because check_lockout/record_failure key on request.client.host — behind K8s ingress this is the ingress/proxy pod IP which rotates across requests (observed 10.64.130.9 and 10.64.129.166 for the same browser). Counter is split, user can attempt unlimited logins. Fix: derive real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first entry) or X-Real-IP header before falling back to request.client.host. Key identifier by email alone for a secondary global lock, or use email-only as identifier.

minor.issue: CORS middleware uses allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL] only; if FRONTEND_URL env is missing or differs from actual origin, credentialed requests will silently fail. Current env is correct but worth documenting.

design_issues.screen: AddressFields (used in Grantor, Trustee, Successor, Beneficiary)
issues: Address inputs (line1/city/state/zip/country) have no data-testid attributes — they use only DOM ids like g-addr-line1. Not a blocker since ids work, but inconsistent with the rest of the wizard which uses data-testid everywhere. Recommend adding testId pass-through in _shared.jsx AddressFields for uniform testability.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout to derive the real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (or key the identifier on email only). Current implementation is effectively bypassed behind the K8s ingress.
(Nice to have) Add data-testid attributes to AddressFields inputs via a testIdPrefix prop for consistent E2E selectors.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py line ~332: `ip = request.client.host` — K8s ingress proxy IP rotates per request across backend pods. Use request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for','').split(',')[0].strip() or x-real-ip as the primary identifier, fall back to request.client.host.

server.py line ~809: CORSMiddleware allow_origins=[FRONTEND_URL] — should read from CORS_ORIGINS env var which is already declared in backend/.env (currently set to '*') but never used. Today credentials cookies work because FRONTEND_URL matches; future misconfiguration risk.

server.py line ~42: `mongo_url = os.environ["MONGO_URL"]` and line 44 `db = client[os.environ["DB_NAME"]]` — fail-fast is good, but startup event also runs create_index which will crash the ASGI app if Mongo is briefly unavailable. Consider lazy index creation or try/except with warning.
server.py put_object/get_object use synchronous `requests` inside async endpoints — will block the event loop on large uploads/downloads. Consider httpx.AsyncClient or asyncio.to_thread.
The /api/trust-cases/{id}/documents/{doc_id}/download endpoint requires login even for simple admin downloads — fine; but there's no link-expiry/signed URL. OK for MVP.
Admin EIN letter upload flow is implicit via doc_type='ein_letter' in the shared upload endpoint; works, but consider a dedicated admin endpoint for clarity.
There's no server-side percentage-sum validation for beneficiaries (>100% allowed). UX validation should be mirrored server-side.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reuse /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py. If brute-force fix lands, the test_brute_force_lockout case will validate it. For UI, key flows verified: register→portal→Single Trust card→wizard, hard-stop + step lock, grantor save unlocks Trustee step, wizard messaging. Not yet exercised end-to-end in UI: full 8-step completion + document upload + EIN auth + Review submit + admin case detail page + branding update from UI. Backend tests already cover each of these per-endpoint.

rca of the issue.bug: Brute force lockout does not activate after 5 failed attempts.
rca of the issue.reproduction: curl /api/auth/login with bad password 6 times for the same (non-existent) email. Expected: 5 × 401 then 429. Actual: 6 × 401. Verified in MongoDB: two login_attempts records were created for the same email under two different IP keys.
rca of the issue.root_cause: server.py uses `ip = request.client.host` to key the per-IP counter. Behind the K8s ingress the request.client.host is the ingress/proxy pod's IP, and there are multiple proxy pods round-robining requests, so attacks are trivially split across keys.
rca of the issue.mitigation: Use X-Forwarded-For (first entry) as the client IP source. Or key on email alone (simpler and still privacy-safe). Ideally use (real_ip, email) with real_ip derived from trusted proxy headers.
